I farm this land the way I know best: I keep the full 16.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the system I have run for years and it fits my well irrigation. I am 76 now, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I will keep things steady and not make the work too complicated. For wheat, I will use an improved seed, put most of the fertilizer on nitrogen with some phosphorus and a little potassium, irrigate two times if water is normal, and use rotary tillage because it saves effort and still gives me a decent seedbed. For maize, I will plant hybrid seed because I care most about stable yield, keep fertilizer strong but not excessive, irrigate two times from the well if the summer rain is not enough, and also use rotary tillage so the field work stays simple and quick. I will spray only as much as I think is needed to control the common diseases, weeds, and insects, because I want the crop protected but I do not want extra cost or extra field passes. My goal this year is not to chase the highest possible yield; I will aim for a stable harvest that matches my labor, my age, and my land conditions.
